newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares shrug off pause, set record gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares shrug off pause, set record gains.

text.p: Germany's DAX index shrugged off expectations on Tuesday for the blue-chip index to take a pause in post-bourse IBIS computer dealings to reach a new all-time record high.
A firmer dollar, which was trading at 1.80 marks in late European dealings, and early gains on Wall Street helped to underpin market sentiment despite lower German debt prices.

"We are really in need of a pause, some sort of consolidation," said one Frankfurt dealer. "People are starting to get nervous and it is becoming hard to justify these sorts of levels and an advance at this pace."

Dealers said the market must begin to consolidate between 4,100 and 4,150 points this week to fend off a nasty bout of profit-taking, which one dealer said could cause the market to do a "backflip" and could push the DAX below 4,000 points.
"Any sort of breather would be welcome but it has to last for more than just a day," said one trader.
The dollar and Wall Street was again the driving forces behind the DAX index, which is heavy on export-sensitive shares that have benefited from their products being cheaper abroad.
Chemicals resumed gains as Hoechst AG was up 1.23 marks to 81.65 marks after setting a new record at 81.74 marks.
Rivals BASF AG was up 85 pfennigs at 68.40 marks and Bayer AG gained 15 pfennigs to 74 marks.
But market darling Volkswagen AG ended bourse trade down 13.50 marks at 1,467.50 marks. VW shares recovered a bit in IBIS dealings to trade at 1,472 marks.
BMW AG was also lower in IBIS dealings, falling 4.65 marks to 1,540.35 marks on profit-taking, while Porsche AG was down 70 marks at 2,800 marks.
Industrial group Viag AG was lower despite saying it expected higher 1997 group sales and for earnings to remain stable or rise slightly during the year.
